newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Confidence resounds at Hong Kong property auction.
newsitem.headline: Confidence resounds at Hong Kong property auction.

text.p: Property developers gave Hong Kong's real estate market an overwhelming vote of confidence on Tuesday by bidding up a plot of land for more than two hours to a record price of more than US$1.5 billion.

Bidding was heated despite concerns over possible government measures to rein in rising housing prices, and also showed no signs of trepidation just three months before the British colony reverts to Chinese sovereignty.

A consortium equally owned by Sino Land Co Ltd and its chairman Robert Ng's family bought the 25,592 square metre plot in Chai Wan for HK$11.82 billion (US$1.53 billion) after a two-hour climb from the opening bid of HK$6.3 billion.
Analysts had expected the site on the eastern side of Hong Kong island, earmarked for non-industrial use, to fetch anywhere between HK$6.0 billion to HK$14.8 billion.
The price was the highest-ever paid for a site at a Hong Kong land auction and the bidding session was also the longest ever, auctioneer and government land agent Herbert Leung said.
"It is certainly a record price," Leung told reporters.
Sino's Ng said his consortium would invest a further HK$20 billion in the development, a commercial and residential complex to be put on the market in two to three years.
Analysts said the price Sino and the Ng family paid was a resounding vote of confidence in the market.
David Faulkner, a partner at property consultancy Brooke Hillier Parker, said Sino Land would have to sell for at least HK$8,000 per square foot to justify what it was paying.
"It means they are looking at a 25 to 30 percent price increase (from current levels)," he said.
Hot competition for the site also heartened analysts.
Market sources said CITIC Pacific Ltd, Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd, Henderson Land Development Co Ltd, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd and New World Development Co Ltd were among the 15 bidders.

"It looks as if all famous locally funded developers took part in the auction," said Tony Chan, managing director at Ricacorp Surveyors Ltd. "This shows that they are very optimistic about the property market in the future."
"Developers don't seem to worry about recent talk that the government will introduce measures (to cool down the property market)," he added.

Secretary for Housing Dominic Wong is scheduled to meet property developers on Wednesday, and the market speculates that the meeting will be aimed at finding ways to further cool speculation that is blamed for the rocketing housing prices.

"I don't think the government will introduce mesaures to make prices fluctuate greatly because steady property prices are greatly conducive to Hong Kong's economy," said New World Development Co Ltd managing director Henry Cheng.
Also at the auction, China Overseas Land and Investment Ltd outbid four competitors to win a plot of 2,627 square metres in Kowloon's Ho Man Tin for HK$1.4 billion.
Industry analysts had expected the residential site to fetch between HK$848 million and HK$1.27 billion.
"We are very delighted with the results and it reflects a good market sentiment," said auctioneer Leung.
"I think naturally what the developers pay reflects the strength of the market and the set of the demand situation at the moment and in the foreseeable future."
